November 2026 119

1 Nov UK

Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down 2026

Directed by Christoph Farwig · 66 min

Unlisted distributor

"Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down" is a documentary film about British social policy. The focus is on the political struggle against neoliberal austerity policies, which have their origins in the hated Thatcher government. The film features the former socialist MP Dave Nellist, who is now the national chair of the Trade Unionist & Socialist Coalition and Hannah Sell, the general secretary of the Socialist Party. The film features a local election campaign in the miners' town of Nuneaton, students campaigning against an increase in tuition fees and refuse workers from Birmingham striking against massive cuts to their wages.

3 Nov UK

Allies in Exile

39 min · Storyville

BBC Storyville

A Storyville documentary that follows Syrian film-makers Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al-Halabi. Having forged a friendship while living through, and filming, the war in Syria, they now face a very different reality as they navigate the UK asylum system. Turning the camera on themselves, they document a new chapter in their own lives shaped by uncertainty, bureaucracy and displacement, offering a deeply personal and very raw exploration of friendship and belonging. This heart-wrenching film offers an intimate perspective on life in exile and the enduring power of storytelling in the face of adversity.

3 Nov UK

An Unknown Substance

40 min · Storyville

BBC Storyville

Vladimir Kara-Murza is a prominent Russian opposition politician and Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist who survived two near-fatal poisonings before being sentenced to 25 years in prison after speaking out against Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. This documentary short follows his wife, Evgenia Kara-Murza, during his imprisonment as she mounts a global campaign to bring him home and ensure that his voice would not be silenced.

3 Nov UK

Of Times There Were Before 2026

Directed by Eshan Sharma · 83 min

Unlisted distributor

Of Times There Were Before is a portrait of Romila Thapar, one of the world’s most influential historians and public intellectuals. At ninety-four, having lived through much of the making of modern India, she stands at an unusual distance from the past she has spent a lifetime studying. The film began with a simple question: who is the person behind the historian’s name? Shot at her home in New Delhi, it is an attempt to encounter Thapar beyond the authority of her work and the public image built around it. What emerges is a portrait of a life still in conversation with its own time.

Inside the Mountain 2026

Directed by Jack Homan · 32 min

Unlisted distributor

In 1988, Paul Eastwood and his climbing partner became the first men to free-climb Britain's deepest open cave shaft, rising from within the UK's largest underground chamber and traversing around its highest unbroken waterfall, three times the height of Niagara falls. The iconic route will have gone unrepeated for almost 40 years. Decades later a new team of climbers, Olympian Molly Thompson-Smith and legend Steve McClure, will tackle the climb once again, hoping to join the few who have ever free-climbed the route.

10 Nov UK

Manhood

99 min · Storyville

BBC Storyville

Dallas businessman Bill Moore aims to make penis enlargement as commonplace as Botox and bring the procedure into the mainstream, positioning male cosmetic surgery as a growing part of the aesthetics industry. The documentary follows several men, including an OnlyFans creator and a father of five, as they put their bodies on the line and undergo surgery in pursuit of physical transformation. Through intimate access to both the practitioners selling the dream and the men buying into it, the film traces the insecurities, trauma and societal pressures driving each of them, while raising uncomfortable questions about the ethics of an industry built on male self-doubt. Filmed over two years, with dark humour and unexpected tenderness, this is a timely and revealing portrait of identity and self-image as cosmetic surgery among men continues to rise.
